root_cause.text: The driver incorrectly performed a combined write-and-read operation for all read transfers in dual/quad modes, causing garbage data to be transmitted over the shared data lines, which bricked the read due to the lack of a dedicated master-out line.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a `dual_quad` flag based on `tx_nbits`/`rx_nbits` and modifies the condition so that `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op` is only called for non-dual/quad transfers; for dual/quad read-only transfers, `mchp_coreqspi_read_op` is used instead. The commit message states that the core handles read clock generation itself and that transmitting garbage data bricks the transfer because QSPI has no dedicated MOSI line.

Date:   Fri Jun 20 14:28:26 2025 +0100

    spi: microchip-core-qspi: Add regular transfers
    
    The driver for CoreQSPI only supports memory operations at present, so
    add support for regular transfers so that the SD card slot and ADC on
    the BeagleV Fire can be used.
    
    Signed-off-by: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
    Co-developed-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: The newly added `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()` function writes dummy data (0xaa) to the TX FIFO when `txbuf` is NULL, which occurs for read-only transfers. In dual/quad modes, the data lines are shared, so this dummy write corrupts the read operation, matching the root cause description of an incorrect combined write-and-read operation for all read transfers.
